memory_candidates.content: Bash pitfall: a function that needs to hand back two values must never be called via $(func ...) command substitution if one of those values is set through a global-variable side effect -- command substitution always forks a subshell, so the side-effect global set inside is silently discarded when the subshell exits, and the caller reads a stale/empty value. Fix: have the function set two (or more) globals and call it as a plain statement in the SAME shell (func "$arg"; use "$GLOBAL_ONE" "$GLOBAL_TWO"), never via $(...). This is easy to miss because the function's PRIMARY classification result (echoed to stdout and captured) looks correct in isolation; only the secondary side-effect value silently breaks.

Reaper self-exclusion pattern for a poll-loop/waiter-shaped process: pid/ppid alone is not enough when the thing being reaped is itself a shape a CALLER might also match (e.g. an orchestrating shell awaiting the reaper). Widen to pid, ppid, process group (pgid), and the full ancestor chain up to PID 1, all computed from ONE already-captured ps -eo snapshot (add pgid to that pass's own field list rather than widening a shared snapshot other passes/tests depend on), and fail closed (warn, reap nothing) if the reaper's own row is missing from the snapshot rather than guessing or falling back to a second query. Detection must never use pgrep -f or ps | grep -- a process whose own command line contains the search pattern will self-match and can kill its own shell (observed real incident, exit 144, twice).
